notes: PSA 4.2 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.06. Prostate volume 69 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.81.

note_sections.t: Ascending prostate-specific antigen levels and a previous positive biopsy necessitate this clinical review.

A 67-year-old mechanical engineer, the patient first registered a prostate-specific antigen level of 2.5 ng/mL during mid-2023. Ongoing surveillance tracked a consistent climb to 4.2 ng/mL, leading to this assessment after an earlier biopsy yielded ISUP Grade Group 1 results. Current complaints include moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, quantified at an IPSS score of 9 out of 35, which remain under conservative management. He resides independently despite being married. A former smoker, he accumulated 30 pack-years before ceasing tobacco use in 2015. His weekly alcohol consumption reaches 31 units, balanced by light weight-training sessions twice each week. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requires tiotropium alongside PRN salbutamol. Recent visits covered gastroenterology for a surveillance colonoscopy, pulmonary function testing, and endocrine screening for thyroid status. He reports mild bilateral hearing loss and requests written consultation summaries. Stable right knee osteoarthritis, stemming from a workplace injury decades ago, also requires management.

DRE — texture: firm and irregular; mobility: fixed; asymmetry: pronounced in the right mid-gland region, consistent with a distinct Nodus. General assessment shows stable vital parameters (blood pressure 113/72 mmHg, heart rate 74 bpm) and clear bilateral lung fields. Peripheral lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly are absent.
